stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( \int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx = 6 \) and \( \int_{5}^{2} f(x)\,dx = -4 \). Find the value of \( \int_{5}^{0} \left(3f(x) + 1\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Join the adjacent intervals: \( \int_{0}^{5} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx + \int_{2}^{5} f(x)\,dx = 6 + (4) = 10 \), since reversing \( \int_{5}^{2} \) changes its sign.
Reverse the requested integral: \( \int_{5}^{0} \left(3f(x) + 1\right) dx = -(3) \int_{0}^{5} f(x)\,dx + (1)(0 - 5) \), and the constant contributes \( -5 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, both a supplied integral and the requested one run right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.A: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.B: given integral from 5 to 2 used as if it ran from 2 to 5
distractor_derivations.C: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
